questions.question_text:
An investor buys $600$ shares with a market price of $\$5.80$ each and pays a flat brokerage fee of $\$28$.
What is the total cost of purchasing the shares?

options.why: Omitted the brokerage fee from the total purchase cost.
Subtracted the brokerage fee instead of adding it.
Added $\$28.80$ instead of the stated $\$28$ brokerage fee.

questions.question_text:
An investor buys $1000$ shares at a market price of $\$4.20$ each.
The brokerage fee is $2\%$.
What is the total cost of purchasing the shares?

options.why: Omitted the brokerage fee.
Subtracted the brokerage fee instead of adding it.
Applied 20% brokerage instead of 2%.

questions.question_text:
An investor sells $450$ shares at a market price of $\$8.40$ each and pays a flat brokerage fee of $\$30$.
What is the net income from the sale?

options.why: Added the brokerage fee instead of subtracting it from sale proceeds.
Omitted the brokerage fee.
Subtracted $\$40$ instead of the stated $\$30$ brokerage fee.

questions.question_text:
An investor sells $800$ shares at a market price of $\$6.50$ each, paying a brokerage fee of $1.5\%$.
What is the net amount received?

options.why: Added the brokerage fee instead of subtracting it from sale proceeds.
Omitted the brokerage fee.
Gave the brokerage fee amount instead of the net proceeds.

questions.question_text:
An investor buys $350$ shares at $\$9.20$ each. The brokerage fee is $1.5\%$.
What is the total cost?

options.why: Omitted the brokerage fee.
Subtracted the $\$48.30$ brokerage fee instead of adding it.
Used 15% brokerage instead of 1.5%.

questions.question_text:
An investor bought $500$ shares at $\$10.00$ each (brokerage $\$20$) and sold them at $\$13.00$ each (brokerage $\$20$).
What was the net profit?

options.why: Ignored brokerage fees on both transactions.
Deducted brokerage on only one of the two transactions.
Added brokerage to proceeds and subtracted from buy cost.

questions.question_text:
A trader bought $250$ shares at $\$16.00$ each and later sold them at $\$20.00$ each. Brokerage fees for buying and selling totalled $\$60$.
What was the profit as a percentage of the cost of the shares before brokerage, correct to two decimal places?

options.why: Ignored the $\$60$ brokerage fees, using $\$1000$ as the profit.
Divided the $\$940$ profit by the $\$5000$ selling share income instead of the $\$4000$ buying share cost.
Deducted the combined $\$60$ brokerage fees twice, using $\$880$ as the profit.

questions.question_text:
An investor bought $1150$ shares at $\$12.48$ each and later sold all the shares at $\$15.26$ each. Brokerage fees for buying and selling totalled $\$112.60$.
What was the net profit?

options.why: Ignored the combined $\$112.60$ brokerage fees.
Deducted the combined $\$112.60$ brokerage fees twice.
Added the combined $\$112.60$ brokerage fees to the difference between selling and buying share values.
